 UCLA earns highest College Football Playoff ranking in school history 
 UCLA coach Bob Chesney shouts across the field during the first half of a win at Minnesota on Saturday. (Abbie Parr / Associated Press) By Los Angeles Times Staff p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text"> Undefeated UCLA has earned its highest College Football Playoff ranking, ascending to No. 4 in the top 25 released Tuesday night.
 The Bruins (9-0) are coming off a decisive 34-20 win at Minnesota and moved up four spots.
 UCLA coach Bob Chesney is accustomed to his team being overlooked during his first season leading the Bruins and has urged the team to ignore all rankings until the final playoff and bowl matchups are set.
 The Bruins have never made the College Football Playoff and never won more than 10 games in a season.

 UCLA, USC pleased as College Football Playoff expands to 24 teams beginning next season 
 USC fans storm the field at the Coliseum after the Trojans’ win over Ohio State on Oct. 31. (Gina Ferazzi/Los Angeles Times) By Iliana Limón Romero ,  Sam Farmer ,  Eddie Pells  and  Connor Dullinger p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text"> GRAPEVINE, Texas —  UCLA and USC scored a win on Monday in their constant fight for respect in the college football rankings that dictate a path to a national championship.
 The Bruins and Trojans rarely are ranked as high as other programs with comparable records, especially those from the Southeastern Conference, in the early College Football Playoff national rankings. Short of going undefeated, USC and UCLA faced limited opportunities to get into what was once a four-team playoff and later expanded to 12 teams. Neither the Trojans nor Bruins have ever made the cut.
 Starting next season, the College Football Playoff will expand to 24 teams, a field so deep that this year’s Bruins and Trojans would be assured spots in the lucrative postseason tournament.

 UCLA moves up to No. 4 in latest AP top 25 poll; USC climbs to No. 15 
 UCLA running back Wayne Knight celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown against Minnesota Saturday in Minneapolis. (Abbie Parr / Associated Press) By Eric Olson p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text"> UCLA is 9-0 for the first time since 1998 and moved up to No. 4 in the latest Associated Press Top 25 poll released Sunday. 
 It’s the Bruins’ highest ranking since their 2001 team was No. 4 following a 6-0 start. 
 While first-year UCLA coach Bob Chesney urged his players to ignore all rankings, including the first round of College Football Playoff rankings that had the Bruins at No. 8, fans have celebrated the move up to No. 4. UCLA is the highest-ranked Big Ten team in the poll.

 Voices Commentary: Undefeated UCLA proves why it should be ranked No. 1 
 UCLA’s Troy Leigber celebrates after blocking a punt during a 34-20 win over Minnesota on Saturday. The Bruins are 9-0. (David Berding / Getty Images) By Bill Plaschke p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text"> This is no longer about sweet underdogs. This is no longer about smoke and mirrors.
 This is as real as a Ty Dieffenbach rocket. This is as legit as a Wayne Knight rumble. This is as true as a Sammy Omosigho roar.
 This is the best college football team in America.
 This is UCLA .
 The College Football Playoff selection committee has insulted them, their city has mostly ignored them, and few outside of the range of Bob Chesney ’s wonderfully gravelly football voice has actually believed in them.
